subject: Post-demo: Clarify econ + CISO checklist, hosting preference & SLOs

Subject: Post-demo: Clarify econ + CISO checklist, hosting preference & SLOs

Hi Mira —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can prioritize the next steps internally and put together a focused commercial + security packet. Attached is a short mutual_action_plan.xlsx and a blank security_questionnaire.pdf to make the procurement handoff easier.

High-level asks (can you confirm / fill in below):
- Primary economic buyer and procurement contact (name + email)
- CISO / security lead who will review a SOC2 + logs package (name + email)
- Target latency SLO: p95 target and token context (e.g., p95 < 300ms for 512 tokens)
- Hosting preference: Hosted API / Redwood Dedicated (reserved) / Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Cost guardrail: any target MSRP or internal cost-per-1M-token budget we should aim for
- Timeline: decision window and any procurement blackout dates

Proposed next steps from our side:
1) We'll prepare a 30-day pilot scope (traffic/capacity assumptions + success metrics).
2) Commercial outline (term, estimated unit economics for pilot and 12mo run-rate).
3) Security evidence bundle (SOC2, audit logs, retention options).

If useful, we can also schedule a short 30-minute call with Rishi to go over latency tradeoffs for different deployment modes.

Thanks — will act quickly once you confirm the items above.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-demo: Clarify econ + CISO checklist, hosting preference & SLOs

Hi Mira — thanks for the quick answers and for looping Dan. A couple of technical clarifications so we size the pilot correctly:
1) Typical prompt + response token counts you expect in production (you said ~256 average — can you confirm breakdown of prompt vs. response?).
2) Concurrency profile: average RPS and expected p95 burst (e.g., average 1.5 RPS, bursts to 6-8 RPS).
3) Are embeddings part of the critical path or used asynchronously (embeddings can change preferred hosting if high QPS).

Based on what you shared, a common Dedicated starter config we propose is 2 reserved instances with NVLink and 120GB usable GPU RAM each (pilot config attached as redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf). For the p95 <= 350ms target at ~256 tokens we typically see p95 in the 180–400ms range depending on batching and KV-cache hit rate; we can target the low end with conservative batching + dedicated KV cache for prompt prefixes.

If you can share a sample trace or histogram of request sizes (even a small CSV), we can run a short bench to give a tighter latency quote. Happy to jump on a 30-min debug session with Dan if helpful.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (stub)

Rishi / Tessa — quick follow-up with the numbers you asked for. Attaching a small sample CSV of anonymized request sizes (via Drive link in-line to keep attachments small).
- Average request: 120 tokens prompt / 160 tokens response (so ~280 tokens total average per call)
- Typical steady-state: ~1.5 RPS
- Peak bursts we've seen on campaigns: up to ~8 RPS for ~3 minute windows
- Embeddings: occasional async jobs, not on the low-latency path right now

Procurement notes:
- Procurement lead will need a draft MSA + commercial outline; they prefer an initial term sheet + pilot appendix.
- Alan Chu will sign off on econ; copying him in case you want to route pricing directly.

Dan — happy to sync if you need anything else on the questionnaire.

Thanks,
Mira
